# TypeScript: two referenced types that share a short name.
#
# TypeScript brings referenced types into a file by name, so a definition that reaches
# `collide.alpha.Vec.1.0` and `collide.beta.Vec.1.0` would import `Vec_1_0` twice -- a duplicate
# identifier, which tsc rejects outright rather than warning about. The generated file simply does
# not compile.
#
# This is ordinary rather than exotic. The standard namespace carries three `Vector3` types and four
# `Scalar` types in sibling `uavcan.si.unit` namespaces, so any definition describing a pose or a
# battery hits it.

# RUN: rm -rf %t && mkdir -p %t
# RUN: %dsdlc --target-language ts %S/fixtures_ts_alias/collide --ts-module collide_demo --outdir %t/ts >/dev/null 2>&1

# The clashing pair is imported under namespace-qualified aliases, for the type and for both runtime
# functions -- they are all derived from the same local name, so they cannot disagree.
# RUN: cat %t/ts/collide/uses_1_0.ts | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=ALIASED

# ALIASED: import { deserializeVec_1_0 as deserializeVec_1_0__collide_alpha, serializeVec_1_0 as serializeVec_1_0__collide_alpha } from "./alpha/vec_1_0";
# ALIASED: import { deserializeVec_1_0 as deserializeVec_1_0__collide_beta, serializeVec_1_0 as serializeVec_1_0__collide_beta } from "./beta/vec_1_0";
# ALIASED: import type { Vec_1_0 as Vec_1_0__collide_alpha } from "./alpha/vec_1_0";
# ALIASED: import type { Vec_1_0 as Vec_1_0__collide_beta } from "./beta/vec_1_0";

# The aliases are what the body refers to, not just what the import line says.
# RUN: cat %t/ts/collide/uses_1_0.ts | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=ALIASED_USE
# ALIASED_USE: from_alpha: Vec_1_0__collide_alpha;
# ALIASED_USE: from_beta: Vec_1_0__collide_beta;

# Aliasing is confined to the clash. A file whose referenced names are already unique imports them
# plainly, so ordinary output is untouched by this.
# RUN: %dsdlc --target-language ts %S/fixtures_docs/demo --ts-module demo_comments --outdir %t/plain >/dev/null 2>&1
# RUN: cat %t/plain/demo/commented_1_0.ts | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=PLAIN
# PLAIN-NOT: as {{[A-Za-z_0-9]+__}}
